title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 12. Mercy to Sarvabhauma
html:
The evening darshan of Jagannatha; Sarvabhauma, taking the Lord for an ordinary man, wishes to invest Him again with the sacred thread and teach Him Vedanta; the Lord reveals to him the hidden meaning of Vedanta, Sarvabhauma falls at His feet and offers prayers, and the Lord embraces him

Verse 1

भुक्त्वा प्रसादं नृहरेः स्वमन्दिरं
प्रविश्य सायं भगवान्ददर्श।
धूपेन सन्धूपितमब्जलोचनं
दीपैरनेकैर्बहुमाल्यकेन॥१॥

bhuktvā prasādaṁ nṛhareḥ svamandiraṁ
praviśya sāyaṁ bhagavāndadarśa|
dhūpena sandhūpitamabjalocanaṁ
dīpairanekairbahumālyakena||1||

bhuktva — having eaten; prasadam — the prasada; nrihareh — of Nrihari; sva-mandiram — into His own temple; pravishya — entering; sayam — in the evening; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dadarsha — beheld; dhupena — with incense; sandhupitam — perfumed; abja-lochanam — the Lotus-eyed; dipaih — with lamps; anekaih — many; bahu-malyakena — with many garlands.

1Having eaten the prasada of Nrihari1, Bhagavan entered His temple in the evening and beheld the Lotus-eyed One, perfumed with incense, lit by many lamps and adorned with many garlands,

Verse 2

विभूषितं पूर्णनिशाधिनाथ-
सहस्रकल्पं नवमेघवर्णम्।
ननाम भूमौ पुरुषोत्तमाख्यं
विकाशिनेत्रेण पपौ मुहुश्च॥२॥

vibhūṣitaṁ pūrṇaniśādhinātha-
sahasrakalpaṁ navameghavarṇam|
nanāma bhūmau puruṣottamākhyaṁ
vikāśinetreṇa papau muhuśca||2||

vibhushitam — adorned; purna-nishadhinatha-sahasra-kalpam — like a thousand full moons; nava-megha-varnam — the colour of a fresh cloud; nanama — bowed down; bhumau — to the ground; purushottama-akhyam — to Him called Purushottama; vikashi-netrena — with wide-open eyes; papau — drank (Him in); muhuh — again and again; cha — and.

2radiant as a thousand full moons, the colour of a fresh rain-cloud. He bowed to the ground before Him who is called Purushottama, and with wide-open eyes drank in His form again and again.

Verse 3

आनन्दराशौ परिमग्नचित्तो
नेत्राम्बुधारातिसुधौतवक्षाः।
रोमाञ्चसञ्चारविभूषिताङ्गो
हेमाद्रिशृङ्गोपमगौरदेहः॥३॥

ānandarāśau parimagnacitto
netrāmbudhārātisudhautavakṣāḥ|
romāñcasañcāravibhūṣitāṅgo
hemādriśṛṅgopamagauradehaḥ||3||

ananda-rashau — in an ocean of bliss; parimagna-chittah — His mind immersed; netra-ambu-dhara-ati-su-dhauta-vakshah — His chest washed by streams of tears; romancha-sanchara-vibhushita-angah — His body adorned with waves of thrilling hair; hema-adri-shringa-upama-gaura-dehah — His golden body like a peak of the golden mountain.

3His mind was immersed in an ocean of bliss, His chest was washed by streams of tears, waves of thrilling hair adorned His body, and His golden form was like a peak of the golden mountain.

Verse 4

रराज राजेव स भूसुराणां
प्रभुः प्रसूनावलिवृष्टिकालम्।
तत्रावसच्छ्रीपुरुषोत्तमं पुन-
र्नत्वा जगामाश्रममाश्रमेशः॥४॥

rarāja rājeva sa bhūsurāṇāṁ
prabhuḥ prasūnāvalivṛṣṭikālam|
tatrāvasacchrīpuruṣottamaṁ puna-
rnatvā jagāmāśramamāśrameśaḥ||4||

raraja — shone; raja — a king; iva — like; sah — He; bhu-suranam — of the brahmanas (gods on earth); prabhuh — the Lord; prasuna-avali-vrishti-kalam — until the time of the shower of flowers; tatra — there; avasat — stayed; shri-purushottamam — to Sri Purushottama; punah — again; natva — bowing; jagama — went; ashramam — to His lodging; ashrama-ishah — the Lord of the ashramas.

4The Lord shone like a king among brahmanas, and He stayed there until the hour when the shower of flowers is offered; then, bowing once more to Sri Purushottama, the Lord of the ashramas2 went back to His lodging.

Verse 5

गत्वा निशायां पुनरेव कीर्तिं
जगौ हरेरद्भुतविक्रमस्य।
स विह्वलः प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यो
लुठन्क्षितौ वेद न चापरं कियत्॥५॥

gatvā niśāyāṁ punareva kīrtiṁ
jagau hareradbhutavikramasya|
sa vihvalaḥ premavibhinnadhairyo
luṭhankṣitau veda na cāparaṁ kiyat||5||

gatva — having gone; nishayam — at night; punah — again; eva — indeed; kirtim — the glory; jagau — sang; hareh — of Hari; adbhuta-vikramasya — of wondrous valour; sah — He; vihvalah — overwhelmed; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered by love; luthan — rolling; kshitau — on the ground; veda — knew; na — not; cha — and; aparam — anything else; kiyat — at all.

5Arriving there, He again sang through the night the glory of Hari of wondrous valour; beside Himself, His composure shattered by love, He rolled on the ground and knew nothing else at all.

Verse 6

एवं महात्मा कतिचिद्दिनानि
तत्रावसत्साधुभिरर्चिताङ्घ्रिः।
अशिक्षयत्सज्जनमब्जनेत्रो
मुदा मनोज्ञैर्वचनामृतैश्च॥६॥

evaṁ mahātmā katiciddināni
tatrāvasatsādhubhirarcitāṅghriḥ|
aśikṣayatsajjanamabjanetro
mudā manojñairvacanāmṛtaiśca||6||

evam — thus; maha-atma — the great soul; katichit — some; dinani — days; tatra — there; avasat — stayed; sadhubhih — by the saintly; archita-anghrih — whose feet were worshipped; ashikshayat — instructed; sat-janam — the good people; abja-netrah — the Lotus-eyed; muda — joyfully; manojnaih — with charming; vachana-amritaih — nectarean words; cha — and.

6Thus the great soul stayed there for some days; the saintly worshipped His feet, and the Lotus-eyed One joyfully instructed the good with the charming nectar of His words.

Verse 7

तस्मिन्कदाचित्परिमोहितात्मा
श्रीसार्वभौमः प्रभुमाययौ सः।
चैतन्यदेवं मनुजं विदित्वा
बभाष ईषन्निजलोकमध्ये॥७॥

tasminkadācitparimohitātmā
śrīsārvabhaumaḥ prabhumāyayau saḥ|
caitanyadevaṁ manujaṁ viditvā
babhāṣa īṣannijalokamadhye||7||

tasmin — then (there); kadachit — once; parimohita-atma — his mind deluded; shri-sarvabhaumah — Sri Sarvabhauma; prabhum — to the Lord; ayayau — came; sah — he; chaitanya-devam — Chaitanyadeva; manujam — a man; viditva — deeming; babhasha — spoke; ishat — a little (a few words); nija-loka-madhye — among his own people.

7Then one day Sri Sarvabhauma, his mind deluded, came to the Lord; taking Chaitanyadeva for an ordinary man, he said a few words among his own people.

Verse 8

स एव मोहोऽपि कृपातिरेकः
श्रीसार्वभौमाय जनार्दनस्य।
यद्यत्करोत्येव हरिः स्वयं प्रभु-
स्तदेव सत्यं जगतो हिताय॥८॥

sa eva moho'pi kṛpātirekaḥ
śrīsārvabhaumāya janārdanasya|
yadyatkarotyeva hariḥ svayaṁ prabhu-
stadeva satyaṁ jagato hitāya||8||

sah — that; eva — very; mohah — delusion; api — even; kripa-atirekah — an excess of mercy; shri-sarvabhaumaya — toward Sri Sarvabhauma; janardanasya — of Janardana; yat yat — whatever; karoti — does; eva — indeed; harih — Hari; svayam — Himself; prabhuh — the Lord; tat — that; eva — alone; satyam — truly; jagatah — of the world; hitaya — for the good.

8Yet even that delusion was an excess of Janardana's mercy toward Sri Sarvabhauma: whatever Hari, the Lord Himself, does is truly for the good of the world.

Verse 9

अयं महावंशसमुद्भवः पुमा-
न्सुपण्डितः स्वल्पवयाः कथं चरेत्।
संन्यासधर्मं तदमुं द्विजं पुनः
कृत्वात्मवेदान्तमशिक्षयामहे॥९॥

ayaṁ mahāvaṁśasamudbhavaḥ pumā-
nsupaṇḍitaḥ svalpavayāḥ kathaṁ caret|
saṁnyāsadharmaṁ tadamuṁ dvijaṁ punaḥ
kṛtvātmavedāntamaśikṣayāmahe||9||

ayam — this; maha-vamsha-samudbhavah — born of a great family; puman — man; su-panditah — a fine scholar; svalpa-vayah — young in years; katham — how; charet — could follow; sannyasa-dharmam — the dharma of sannyasa; tat — therefore; amum — him; dvijam — twice-born; punah — again; kritva — making; atma-vedantam — the Vedanta of the Self; ashikshayamahe — let us teach.

9"This man is born of a great family and is a fine scholar, but He is so young — how can He keep the dharma of sannyasa? Let us make Him twice-born again and teach Him the Vedanta of the Self."3

Verse 10

ज्ञात्वा हरिस्तत्पुनराह सस्मितो
यज्ञोपवीतं पुनरेव मे भवेत्।
पुष्पाणि पूगान्यनुगन्धवन्ति
माल्यानि विप्राय ददाम्यहं तदा॥१०॥

jñātvā haristatpunarāha sasmito
yajñopavītaṁ punareva me bhavet|
puṣpāṇi pūgānyanugandhavanti
mālyāni viprāya dadāmyahaṁ tadā||10||

jnatva — learning; harih — Hari; tat — that; punah — in reply; aha — said; sa-smitah — with a smile; yajna-upavitam — the sacred thread; punah — again; eva — indeed; me — to Me; bhavet — let there be; pushpani — flowers; pugani — betel nuts; anugandhavanti — fragrant; malyani — garlands; vipraya — to the brahmana; dadami — will give; aham — I; tada — then.

10Learning of this, Hari answered with a smile, "Let Me be given the sacred thread again — then I shall present the brahmana with flowers, betel nuts and fragrant garlands."4

Verse 11

इत्याह गत्वा वचनं मुरारेः
श्रीसार्वभौमाय जनो विदित्वा।
भीत्या न किञ्चित्पुनरेवमूचे
व्रीडापरोऽभूत्स तु सम्भ्रमेण॥११॥

ityāha gatvā vacanaṁ murāreḥ
śrīsārvabhaumāya jano viditvā|
bhītyā na kiñcitpunarevamūce
vrīḍāparo'bhūtsa tu sambhrameṇa||11||

iti — thus; aha — told; gatva — going; vachanam — the words; murareh — of Murari (the Lord); shri-sarvabhaumaya — to Sri Sarvabhauma; janah — someone; viditva — learning; bhitya — out of fear; na — not; kinchit — anything; punah — again; evam — thus; uche — said; vrida-parah — full of shame; abhut — became; sah — he; tu — but; sambhramena — with confusion.

11Someone who heard these words of Murari5 went and repeated them to Sri Sarvabhauma; and he, out of fear, never said anything of the kind again, but was confused and full of shame.

Verse 12

अथापराह्णे द्विजवृन्दसन्निधौ
स सार्वभौमस्य पुरो महाप्रभुः।
उवाच वेदान्तनिगूढमर्थं
वचो मुरारेश्चरणाम्बुजाश्रयम्॥१२॥

athāparāhṇe dvijavṛndasannidhau
sa sārvabhaumasya puro mahāprabhuḥ|
uvāca vedāntanigūḍhamarthaṁ
vaco murāreścaraṇāmbujāśrayam||12||

atha — then; apara-ahne — in the afternoon; dvija-vrinda-sannidhau — in the presence of many brahmanas; sah — He; sarvabhaumasya — of Sarvabhauma; purah — before; maha-prabhuh — Mahaprabhu; uvacha — spoke; vedanta-nigudham — hidden in Vedanta; artham — the meaning; vachah — a word; murareh — of Murari; charana-ambuja-ashrayam — about shelter at the lotus feet.

12Then one afternoon, in the presence of many brahmanas, before Sarvabhauma, Mahaprabhu set forth the hidden meaning of Vedanta — the teaching of shelter at the lotus feet of Murari.

Verse 13

वेदान्तसिद्धान्तमिदं विदित्वा
गतं पुरा यत्तदलं स मत्वा।
चैतन्यपादाब्जयुगे महात्मा
स विस्मयोत्फुल्लमनाः पपात॥१३॥

vedāntasiddhāntamidaṁ viditvā
gataṁ purā yattadalaṁ sa matvā|
caitanyapādābjayuge mahātmā
sa vismayotphullamanāḥ papāta||13||

vedanta-siddhantam — conclusion of Vedanta; idam — this; viditva — understanding; gatam — gone; pura — before; yat — what; tat — that; alam — enough (worthless); sah — he; matva — deeming; chaitanya-pada-abja-yuge — at the pair of Chaitanya's lotus feet; maha-atma — the great soul; sah — he; vismaya-utphulla-manah — his mind blossoming with wonder; papata — fell.

13Understanding this conclusion of Vedanta and counting all he had known before as worthless, the great soul Sarvabhauma, his mind blossoming with wonder, fell at Chaitanya's lotus feet.

Verse 14

वेदानुरक्तो भगवान्भवान्प्रभु-
र्लोको न जानाति कदाचिदप्यपि।
सम्मोहितात्मा तव मायया प्रभो
लोके पदाब्जं च तवाहमग्रतः॥१४॥

vedānurakto bhagavānbhavānprabhu-
rloko na jānāti kadācidapyapi|
sammohitātmā tava māyayā prabho
loke padābjaṁ ca tavāhamagrataḥ||14||

veda-anuraktah — devoted to the Vedas; bhagavan — Bhagavan; bhavan — You; prabhuh — the Lord; lokah — the world; na — not; janati — knows; kadachit api — ever; api — even; sammohita-atma — my mind deluded; tava — by Your; mayaya — maya; prabho — O Lord; loke — in the world; pada-abjam — the lotus feet; cha — and; tava — Your; aham — I; agratah — before me.

14"You are Bhagavan, the Lord who loves the Vedas, yet the world never knows You; and I too, my mind clouded by Your maya, O Lord, did not recognise Your lotus feet that had appeared in the world right before me.

Verse 15

पुरा पृथिव्यां वसुदेवगेहे-
ऽवतीर्य कंसादिमहासुराणाम्।
कृत्वा वधं त्वं प्रतिपाद्य धाम
भूदेवगेहे पुनराविरासीत्॥१५॥

purā pṛthivyāṁ vasudevagehe-
'vatīrya kaṁsādimahāsurāṇām|
kṛtvā vadhaṁ tvaṁ pratipādya dhāma
bhūdevagehe punarāvirāsīt||15||

pura — once; prithivyam — on earth; vasudeva-gehe — in the house of Vasudeva; avatirya — having descended; kamsa-adi-maha-asuranam — of the great asuras headed by Kamsa; kritva — accomplishing; vadham — the slaying; tvam — You; pratipadya — having reached; dhama — Your abode; bhu-deva-gehe — in the house of a brahmana; punah — again; avirasit — have appeared.

15Once You descended to earth in the house of Vasudeva and slew the great asuras headed by Kamsa; then, having returned to Your abode, You have appeared again in the house of a brahmana.

Verse 16

स्वकीयमाधुर्यविलासवैभव-
मास्वादयंस्त्वं स्वजनं सुखाय च।
कृतावतारो जगतः शिवाय
मां पाहि दीनं करुणामृताब्धे॥१६॥

svakīyamādhuryavilāsavaibhava-
māsvādayaṁstvaṁ svajanaṁ sukhāya ca|
kṛtāvatāro jagataḥ śivāya
māṁ pāhi dīnaṁ karuṇāmṛtābdhe||16||

svakiya-madhurya-vilasa-vaibhavam — the splendour of the play of Your own sweetness; asvadayan — letting taste; tvam — You; sva-janam — Your own people; sukhaya — for joy; cha — and; krita-avatarah — having descended; jagatah — of the world; shivaya — for the good; mam — me; pahi — protect; dinam — wretched; karuna-amrita-abdhe — O ocean of the nectar of compassion.

16You have descended for the good of the world, to let Your own people taste the splendour of the play of Your sweetness and to give them joy. Protect me, wretched as I am, O ocean of the nectar of compassion!

Verse 17

वैराग्यविद्यानिजभक्तियोग-
शिक्षार्थमेकः पुरुषः पुराणः।
श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यशरीरधारी
कृपाम्बुधिर्यस्तमहं प्रपद्ये॥१७॥

vairāgyavidyānijabhaktiyoga-
śikṣārthamekaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ|
śrīkṛṣṇacaitanyaśarīradhārī
kṛpāmbudhiryastamahaṁ prapadye||17||

vairagya-vidya-nija-bhakti-yoga-shiksha-artham — to teach renunciation, knowledge and the yoga of devotion to Himself; ekah — the one; purushah — Person; puranah — primeval; shri-krishna-chaitanya-sharira-dhari — bearing the form of Sri Krishna Chaitanya; kripa-ambudhih — the ocean of mercy; yah — who; tam — in Him; aham — I; prapadye — take refuge.

17The one primeval Person, an ocean of mercy, has taken the form of Sri Krishna Chaitanya to teach renunciation, knowledge and the yoga of devotion to Himself. In Him I take refuge.

Verse 18

कालान्नष्टं भक्तियोगं निजं यः
प्रादुष्कर्तुं कृष्णचैतन्यनामा।
आविर्भूतस्तस्य पादारविन्दे
गाढं गाढं लीयतां चित्तभृङ्गः॥१८॥

kālānnaṣṭaṁ bhaktiyogaṁ nijaṁ yaḥ
prāduṣkartuṁ kṛṣṇacaitanyanāmā|
āvirbhūtastasya pādāravinde
gāḍhaṁ gāḍhaṁ līyatāṁ cittabhṛṅgaḥ||18||

kalat — through time; nashtam — lost; bhakti-yogam — the yoga of devotion; nijam — His own; yah — who; pradushkartum — to make manifest again; krishna-chaitanya-nama — named Krishna Chaitanya; avirbhutah — has appeared; tasya — His; pada-aravinde — in the lotus feet; gadham gadham — deeper and deeper; liyatam — may it be absorbed; chitta-bhringah — the bee of the mind.

18He has appeared under the name of Krishna Chaitanya to make manifest once more the yoga of devotion to Himself, lost with the passage of time. May the bee of my mind sink deeper and deeper into His lotus feet!"6

Verse 19

इति निगदितवन्तं सार्वभौमं करेण
सरसमतिजवेन स्नेहभावेन धृत्वा।
निजहृदि विनिधायालिङ्गनं स प्रचक्रे
वरभुजयुगलेन श्रीपतिर्भक्तवश्यः॥१९॥

iti nigaditavantaṁ sārvabhaumaṁ kareṇa
sarasamatijavena snehabhāvena dhṛtvā|
nijahṛdi vinidhāyāliṅganaṁ sa pracakre
varabhujayugalena śrīpatirbhaktavaśyaḥ||19||

iti — thus; nigaditavantam — who had spoken; sarvabhaumam — Sarvabhauma; karena — by the hand; sa-rasam — with feeling; ati-javena — swiftly; sneha-bhavena — with affection; dhritva — taking; nija-hridi — to His heart; vinidhaya — pressing; alinganam — an embrace; sah — He; prachakre — gave; vara-bhuja-yugalena — with His two beautiful arms; shri-patih — the Husband of Shri; bhakta-vashyah — submissive to His devotees.

19When Sarvabhauma had spoken thus, the Husband of Shri, who submits to His devotees, impulsively, with feeling and tenderness, took him by the hand, pressed him to His heart and embraced him with His two beautiful arms.

Thus ends the twelfth sarga, "Mercy to Sarvabhauma" (Sarvabhauma-anugraha), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Nrihari ("Hari in human form"): here Jagannatha.
  2. The Lord of the ashramas: the Lord as a sannyasi, in the highest of the four ashramas.
  3. "The Vedanta of the Self" (atma-vedanta) is the teaching of Advaita (Mayavada), which Sarvabhauma then held: that the self is one with the impersonal Brahman. The poet plainly calls this intention a delusion (vv. 7–8); the true, "hidden meaning of Vedanta" is shelter at the Lord's lotus feet (v. 12), and on grasping it Sarvabhauma counts his former knowledge worthless (v. 13).
  4. The Lord's playful reply: at the investiture the pupil presents gifts to his brahmana teacher.
  5. Here Murari ("Enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna, that is, of the Lord Himself.
  6. Verses 17–18 are also quoted as Sarvabhauma's prayer in Krishnadasa Kaviraja's "Chaitanya Charitamrita" (Madhya 6.254–255).
